(ns stock.core-spec
  "The contract for stock.core: lots of goods with expiry dates, and the
  few things that can happen to them.

  A lot is usable at a tick `now` when it is :active, holds at least one
  unit, and has not reached its :expires. Every law is written against the
  spec's own vocabulary (`usable?`, `live`), never against the code.

  Boundaries the laws anchor: `now` at :expires is expired (`<`, not
  `<=`), a lot of qty 0 is not usable, `take-from` may take exactly the
  whole lot (which removes it) but not one more, and `purge` takes a lot
  whose :expires equals `now` while `available` does not count it."
  (:require [writ.spec :refer [spec ann law graph refine example]]))

(spec stock.core)

;; --- types ----------------------------------------------------------------------

(refine Status [s Keyword] (contains? #{:active :quarantined} s))

(refine Lot [l {:id Nat, :sku Nat, :qty Nat, :expires Nat, :status Status}] true)

(refine Stock [s {:lots (Index :id Lot), :next-id Nat}] true)

(ann receive    [Stock Nat Nat Nat -> (Tuple Stock (Opt Nat))])
(ann available  [Stock Nat Nat -> Nat])
(ann quarantine [Stock Nat -> Stock])
(ann release    [Stock Nat -> Stock])
(ann take-from  [Stock Nat Nat Nat -> (Tuple Stock Bool)])
(ann purge      [Stock Nat -> Stock])

;; --- the spec's own vocabulary ---------------------------------------------------

(defn usable?
  "Is lot usable at `now`?  :active, at least one unit, not yet expired."
  [lot now]
  (and (= :active (:status lot))
       (pos? (:qty lot))
       (< now (:expires lot))))

(defn live
  "The usable lots of `sku` in `stock` at `now`."
  [stock sku now]
  (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %)) (usable? % now)) (vals (:lots stock))))

;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------------

;; receive hands back a stock and the new id; take-from hands back a stock
;; and its verdict.  Taking the stock back out of either lands in :stock.
(graph stock
  {:states {:stock     Stock
            :available Nat
            :received  (Tuple Stock (Opt Nat))
            :taken     (Tuple Stock Bool)}
   :edges  {:stock     {[receive Nat Nat Nat]  #{:received}
                        [available Nat Nat]   #{:available}
                        [quarantine Nat]      #{:stock}
                        [release Nat]         #{:stock}
                        [take-from Nat Nat Nat] #{:taken}
                        [purge Nat]           #{:stock}}
            :received  {[first] #{:stock}}
            :taken     {[first] #{:stock}}}})

;; --- receiving -------------------------------------------------------------------

(law receive-adds-an-active-lot
  (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, qty Nat, expires Nat]
    (=> (pos? qty)
        (let [[s2 id] (receive s sku qty expires)]
          (and (= id (:next-id s))
               (= (inc (:next-id s)) (:next-id s2))
               (= (assoc (:lots s) id
                         {:id id :sku sku :qty qty :expires expires :status :active})
                  (:lots s2)))))))

(law receive-of-nothing-is-nothing
  (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, expires Nat]
    (= [s nil] (receive s sku 0 expires))))

;; --- counting what is available --------------------------------------------------

(law available-counts-the-usable-lots
  (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, now Nat]
    (= (available s sku now)
       (reduce + 0 (map :qty (live s sku now))))))

;; --- holding a lot back and letting it go ----------------------------------------

(law quarantine-marks-the-lot
  (forall [s Stock, id Nat]
    (let [l (get (:lots s) id)]
      (= (quarantine s id)
         (if (some? l)
           (assoc s :lots (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :status :quarantined)))
           s)))))

(law release-reactivates-a-quarantined-lot
  (forall [s Stock, id Nat]
    (let [l (get (:lots s) id)
          held (and (some? l) (= :quarantined (:status l)))]
      (= (release s id)
         (if held
           (assoc s :lots (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :status :active)))
           s)))))

;; --- taking units out ------------------------------------------------------------

(law take-from-takes-when-it-may
  (forall [s Stock, id Nat, n Nat, now Nat]
    (let [l (get (:lots s) id)
          can (and (some? l) (usable? l now) (<= 1 n) (<= n (:qty l)))]
      (= (take-from s id n now)
         (if can
           (let [q (- (:qty l) n)
                 lots (if (zero? q)
                        (dissoc (:lots s) id)
                        (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :qty q)))]
             [(assoc s :lots lots) true])
           [s false])))))

;; --- clearing the shelf ----------------------------------------------------------

(law purge-drops-the-expired
  (forall [s Stock, now Nat]
    (= (purge s now)
       (assoc s :lots
              (into {} (remove (fn [[_ l]] (<= (:expires l) now)) (:lots s)))))))

;; --- examples at the boundaries --------------------------------------------------

(def empty-stock {:lots {} :next-id 0})

(def one-lot
  {:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :active}}
   :next-id 2})

;; qty 0 leaves the stock and the id alone
(example receive [empty-stock 7 0 20] [empty-stock nil])

;; qty 1 adds the lot under :next-id and moves :next-id on
(example receive [empty-stock 7 5 20]
         [{:lots {0 {:id 0 :sku 7 :qty 5 :expires 20 :status :active}} :next-id 1}
          0])

;; a lot is usable just before it expires ...
(example available [one-lot 4 9] 3)
;; ... and not at :expires
(example available [one-lot 4 10] 0)
;; a quarantined lot is not usable
(example available [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :quarantined}}
                     :next-id 2} 4 9] 0)
;; an empty lot is not usable
(example available [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 0 :expires 10 :status :active}}
                     :next-id 2} 4 9] 0)
;; another sku's lot is not counted
(example available [one-lot 5 9] 0)

;; taking exactly the lot removes it
(example take-from [one-lot 1 3 9] [{:lots {} :next-id 2} true])
;; taking one more than it holds is refused
(example take-from [one-lot 1 4 9] [one-lot false])
;; taking none is refused
(example take-from [one-lot 1 0 9] [one-lot false])
;; taking at :expires is refused
(example take-from [one-lot 1 1 10] [one-lot false])
;; a partial take leaves the rest
(example take-from [one-lot 1 2 9]
         [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 1 :expires 10 :status :active}} :next-id 2} true])

;; purge takes a lot at its expiry, whatever its status
(example purge [one-lot 10] {:lots {} :next-id 2})
(example purge [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :quarantined}}
                 :next-id 2} 10]
         {:lots {} :next-id 2})
(example purge [one-lot 9] one-lot)

(ns picking.core-spec
  "The contract for picking.core, built on stock.core's spec.

  A plan is the picks that would take n of a sku: first-expiring-first,
  lowest id on a tie, each lot used up before the next is touched, the
  last pick only what is still needed, [] for n 0, nil when the usable
  lots hold less than n.  `pick` fills an order line by line through the
  component's take-from.

  What the component means is said here in the spec's own words
  (`model-plan`, `model-pick`), which do not call the component's fns, so
  this spec loads and checks before stock.core is written.  The target's
  own code must reach stock.core/take-from to fill a line."
  (:require [writ.spec :refer [spec ann law graph refine example calls]]))

(spec picking.core {:uses [stock.core-spec]})

;; --- types ----------------------------------------------------------------------

(refine Line [l {:sku Nat, :qty Nat}] true)

(refine Report [r {:filled (Vec Nat)
                   :short  (Vec Nat)
                   :picks  (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat Nat))}] true)

(ann plan [Stock Nat Nat Nat -> (Opt (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))])
(ann pick [Stock (Vec Line) Nat -> (Tuple Stock Report)])

;; --- the component's meaning in this spec's own words ----------------------------

(defn usable?
  "Is lot usable at `now`?  :active, at least one unit, not yet expired."
  [lot now]
  (and (= :active (:status lot))
       (pos? (:qty lot))
       (< now (:expires lot))))

(defn live
  "The usable lots of `sku` in `stock` at `now`."
  [stock sku now]
  (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %)) (usable? % now)) (vals (:lots stock))))

(defn ordered
  "Earliest to expire first; on a tie, the lowest id."
  [lots]
  (sort-by (juxt :expires :id) lots))

(defn model-plan
  "The picks that would take n of sku: [] for n 0, nil when short, else
  each usable lot in order used up, the last taking only what is needed."
  [stock sku n now]
  (if (zero? n)
    []
    (let [[picks left]
          (reduce (fn [[acc need] l]
                    (if (pos? need)
                      (let [k (min need (:qty l))]
                        [(conj acc [(:id l) k]) (- need k)])
                      [acc need]))
                  [[] n]
                  (ordered (live stock sku now)))]
      (if (pos? left) nil picks))))

(defn model-take
  "The component's take-from on a lots map, as a lot map again: the qty
  drops, and a lot reaching 0 is removed."
  [lots id k]
  (let [l (get lots id)
        q (- (:qty l) k)]
    (if (zero? q)
      (dissoc lots id)
      (assoc lots id (assoc l :qty q)))))

(defn model-pick
  "The order filled line by line against the model above.  A line whose
  plan is nil is short and takes nothing; its picks are tagged with its
  index, in the order they were made."
  [stock order now]
  (loop [i 0
         lots (:lots stock)
         filled []
         short []
         picks []]
    (if (< i (count order))
      (let [line (nth order i)
            p (model-plan (assoc stock :lots lots) (:sku line) (:qty line) now)]
        (if (nil? p)
          (recur (inc i) lots filled (conj short i) picks)
          (let [[lots2 picks2]
                (reduce (fn [[ls ps] [id k]]
                          [(model-take ls id k) (conj ps [i id k])])
                        [lots picks]
                        p)]
            (recur (inc i) lots2 (conj filled i) short picks2))))
      [(assoc stock :lots lots)
       {:filled filled :short short :picks picks}])))

;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------------

(graph picking
  {:states {:stock Stock
            :plan  (Opt (Vec (Tuple Nat Nat)))
            :picked (Tuple Stock Report)}
   :edges  {:stock  {[plan Nat Nat Nat]     #{:plan}
                     [pick (Vec Line) Nat]  #{:picked}}
            :picked {[first] #{:stock}}}})

;; --- the target must fill through the component ----------------------------------

(calls pick {:through [stock.core/take-from]})

;; --- the laws --------------------------------------------------------------------

(law plan-is-the-greedy-first-expiring
  (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, n Nat, now Nat]
    (= (plan s sku n now) (model-plan s sku n now))))

(law pick-fills-every-line-it-can
  (forall [s Stock, order (Vec Line), now Nat]
    (= (pick s order now) (model-pick s order now))))

;; --- examples at the boundaries --------------------------------------------------

(def empty-stock {:lots {} :next-id 0})

(def two-lots
  {:lots {2 {:id 2 :sku 4 :qty 5 :expires 10 :status :active}
          1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :active}}
   :next-id 3})

;; n 0 is the empty plan, even with nothing in stock
(example plan [empty-stock 4 0 0] [])
;; short: fewer usable units than asked
(example plan [empty-stock 4 1 0] nil)
;; a tie on :expires goes to the lowest id; that lot is used up first
(example plan [two-lots 4 4 9] [[1 3] [2 1]])
;; the whole lot exactly: one pick, used up
(example plan [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :active}} :next-id 2} 4 3 9]
         [[1 3]])
;; a quarantined lot is not planned
(example plan [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :quarantined}} :next-id 2} 4 1 9]
         nil)
;; an empty order fills to an empty report and leaves the stock
(example pick [two-lots [] 9] [two-lots {:filled [] :short [] :picks []}])
;; a short line takes nothing and the next line goes on
(example pick [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 1 :expires 10 :status :active}
                       2 {:id 2 :sku 5 :qty 2 :expires 10 :status :active}}
                :next-id 3}
               [{:sku 4 :qty 2} {:sku 5 :qty 1}] 9]
         [{:lots {2 {:id 2 :sku 5 :qty 1 :expires 10 :status :active}} :next-id 3}
          {:filled [1] :short [0] :picks [[1 2 1]]}])
;; a line of qty 0 is filled, with no picks
(example pick [two-lots [{:sku 4 :qty 0}] 9]
         [two-lots {:filled [0] :short [] :picks []}])

(ns stock.core
  "Lots of goods with expiry dates, and the few things that happen to them.
  Time is a Nat tick passed in; nothing reads a clock.")

(defn- usable?
  "A lot is usable at `now` when it is :active, holds at least one unit,
  and has not reached its :expires."
  [lot now]
  (and (= :active (:status lot))
       (pos? (:qty lot))
       (< now (:expires lot))))

(defn receive
  "Add an :active lot of `qty` of `sku`, expiring at `expires`.  A qty of 0
  changes nothing and gives no id."
  [stock sku qty expires]
  (if (pos? qty)
    (let [id (:next-id stock)
          lot {:id id :sku sku :qty qty :expires expires :status :active}]
      [(assoc stock
              :lots (assoc (:lots stock) id lot)
              :next-id (inc id))
       id])
    [stock nil]))

(defn available
  "The total qty of the usable lots of `sku` at `now`."
  [stock sku now]
  (reduce + 0
          (map :qty
               (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %)) (usable? % now))
                       (vals (:lots stock))))))

(defn quarantine
  "Hold lot `id` back.  With no such lot, nothing changes."
  [stock id]
  (if (contains? (:lots stock) id)
    (assoc stock :lots
           (assoc (:lots stock) id
                  (assoc (get (:lots stock) id) :status :quarantined)))
    stock))

(defn release
  "Make a quarantined lot `id` active again.  Anything else changes nothing."
  [stock id]
  (let [lot (get (:lots stock) id)]
    (if (and (some? lot) (= :quarantined (:status lot)))
      (assoc stock :lots (assoc (:lots stock) id (assoc lot :status :active)))
      stock)))

(defn take-from
  "Take `n` from usable lot `id`.  Its qty drops, a lot reaching 0 is
  removed, and `ok?` is true; otherwise nothing changes and `ok?` is false."
  [stock id n now]
  (let [lot (get (:lots stock) id)]
    (if (and (some? lot) (usable? lot now) (<= 1 n) (<= n (:qty lot)))
      (let [q (- (:qty lot) n)]
        [(assoc stock :lots
                (if (zero? q)
                  (dissoc (:lots stock) id)
                  (assoc (:lots stock) id (assoc lot :qty q))))
         true])
      [stock false])))

(defn purge
  "Remove every lot that has expired (`:expires <= now`), whatever its status."
  [stock now]
  (assoc stock :lots
         (reduce-kv (fn [m id lot]
                      (if (<= (:expires lot) now) m (assoc m id lot)))
                    {}
                    (:lots stock))))

(ns picking.core
  "Fill orders from stock.core: plan what to take first-expiring-first, and
  pick it through the component."
  (:require [stock.core :as stock]))

(defn- usable?
  [lot now]
  (and (= :active (:status lot))
       (pos? (:qty lot))
       (< now (:expires lot))))

(defn- live
  "The usable lots of `sku` in `stock` at `now`."
  [stock sku now]
  (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %)) (usable? % now)) (vals (:lots stock))))

(defn- ordered
  "Earliest to expire first; on a tie, the lowest id."
  [lots]
  (sort-by (juxt :expires :id) lots))

(defn plan
  "The picks that would take `n` of `sku`: first-expiring-first, each lot
  used up before the next, the last taking only what is still needed.  []
  for n 0, nil when the usable lots hold less than n in all."
  [stock sku n now]
  (if (zero? n)
    []
    (let [[picks left]
          (reduce (fn [[acc need] lot]
                    (if (pos? need)
                      (let [k (min need (:qty lot))]
                        [(conj acc [(:id lot) k]) (- need k)])
                      [acc need]))
                  [[] n]
                  (ordered (live stock sku now)))]
      (if (pos? left) nil picks))))

(defn- fill-line
  "Fill `line` at index `i` through the component, tagging each pick with
  the index.  A line whose plan is nil is short and takes nothing."
  [stock report i line now]
  (if-let [p (plan stock (:sku line) (:qty line) now)]
    (let [[s picks]
          (reduce (fn [[s ps] [id k]]
                    (let [[s2 _] (stock/take-from s id k now)]
                      [s2 (conj ps [i id k])]))
                  [stock (:picks report)]
                  p)]
      [s (assoc report
                :filled (conj (:filled report) i)
                :picks picks)])
    [stock (assoc report :short (conj (:short report) i))]))

(defn pick
  "Fill `order`, a vector of lines, in order.  Each line takes its plan's
  picks through stock.core/take-from; a short line takes nothing and the
  next lines go on.  Returns [stock' report]."
  [stock order now]
  (reduce (fn [[s report] [i line]]
            (fill-line s report i line now))
          [stock {:filled [] :short [] :picks []}]
          (map-indexed (fn [i line] [i line]) order)))

39:        (< now (:expires lot))))
40: 
41: (defn live
42:   "The usable lots of `sku` in `stock` at `now`."
43:   [stock sku now]
44:   (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %)) (usable? % now)) (vals (:lots stock))))
45: 
46: ;; --- the state graph -------------------------------------------------------------
47: 
48: ;; receive hands back a stock and the new id; take-from hands back a stock
49: ;; and its verdict.  Taking the stock back out of either lands in :stock.
50: (graph stock
51:   {:states {:stock     Stock
52:             :available Nat
53:             :received  (Tuple Stock (Opt Nat))
54:             :taken     (Tuple Stock Bool)}
55:    :edges  {:stock     {[receive Nat Nat Nat]  #{:received}
56:                         [available Nat Nat]   #{:available}
57:                         [quarantine Nat]      #{:stock}
58:                         [release Nat]         #{:stock}
59:                         [take-from Nat Nat Nat] #{:taken}
60:                         [purge Nat]           #{:stock}}
61:             :received  {[first] #{:stock}}
62:             :taken     {[first] #{:stock}}}})
63: 
64: ;; --- receiving -------------------------------------------------------------------
65: 
66: (law receive-adds-an-active-lot
67:   (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, qty Nat, expires Nat]
68:     (=> (pos? qty)
69:         (let [[s2 id] (receive s sku qty expires)]
70:           (and (= id (:next-id s))
71:                (= (inc (:next-id s)) (:next-id s2))
72:                (= (assoc (:lots s) id
73:                          {:id id :sku sku :qty qty :expires expires :status :active})
74:                   (:lots s2)))))))
75: 
76: (law receive-of-nothing-is-nothing
77:   (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, expires Nat]
78:     (= [s nil] (receive s sku 0 expires))))
79: 
80: ;; --- counting what is available --------------------------------------------------
81: 
82: (law available-counts-the-usable-lots
83:   (forall [s Stock, sku Nat, now Nat]
84:     (= (available s sku now)
85:        (reduce + 0 (map :qty (live s sku now))))))
86: 
87: ;; --- holding a lot back and letting it go ----------------------------------------
88: 
89: (law quarantine-marks-the-lot
90:   (forall [s Stock, id Nat]
91:     (let [l (get (:lots s) id)]
92:       (= (quarantine s id)
93:          (if (some? l)
94:            (assoc s :lots (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :status :quarantined)))
95:            s)))))
96: 
97: (law release-reactivates-a-quarantined-lot
98:   (forall [s Stock, id Nat]
99:     (let [l (get (:lots s) id)
100:           held (and (some? l) (= :quarantined (:status l)))]
101:       (= (release s id)
102:          (if held
103:            (assoc s :lots (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :status :active)))
104:            s)))))
105: 
106: ;; --- taking units out ------------------------------------------------------------
107: 
108: (law take-from-takes-when-it-may
109:   (forall [s Stock, id Nat, n Nat, now Nat]
110:     (let [l (get (:lots s) id)
111:           can (and (some? l) (usable? l now) (<= 1 n) (<= n (:qty l)))]
112:       (= (take-from s id n now)
113:          (if can
114:            (let [q (- (:qty l) n)
115:                  lots (if (zero? q)
116:                         (dissoc (:lots s) id)
117:                         (assoc (:lots s) id (assoc l :qty q)))]
118:              [(assoc s :lots lots) true])
119:            [s false])))))
120: 
121: ;; --- clearing the shelf ----------------------------------------------------------
122: 
123: (law purge-drops-the-expired
124:   {:require :tested
125:    :because "purge folds a map of unknown size; the prover does not model the fold and found no proof"}
126:   (forall [s Stock, now Nat]
127:     (= (purge s now)
128:        (assoc s :lots
129:               (into {} (remove (fn [[_ l]] (<= (:expires l) now)) (:lots s)))))))
130: 
131: ;; --- examples at the boundaries --------------------------------------------------
132: 
133: (def empty-stock {:lots {} :next-id 0})
134: 
135: (def one-lot
136:   {:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :active}}
137:    :next-id 2})
138: 
139: ;; qty 0 leaves the stock and the id alone
140: (example receive [empty-stock 7 0 20] [empty-stock nil])
141: 
142: ;; qty 1 adds the lot under :next-id and moves :next-id on
143: (example receive [empty-stock 7 5 20]
144:          [{:lots {0 {:id 0 :sku 7 :qty 5 :expires 20 :status :active}} :next-id 1}
145:           0])
146: 
147: ;; a lot is usable just before it expires ...
148: (example available [one-lot 4 9] 3)
149: ;; ... and not at :expires
150: (example available [one-lot 4 10] 0)
151: ;; a quarantined lot is not usable
152: (example available [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :quarantined}}
153:                      :next-id 2} 4 9] 0)
154: ;; an empty lot is not usable
155: (example available [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 0 :expires 10 :status :active}}
156:                      :next-id 2} 4 9] 0)
157: ;; another sku's lot is not counted
158: (example available [one-lot 5 9] 0)
159: 
160: ;; taking exactly the lot removes it
161: (example take-from [one-lot 1 3 9] [{:lots {} :next-id 2} true])
162: ;; taking one more than it holds is refused
163: (example take-from [one-lot 1 4 9] [one-lot false])
164: ;; taking none is refused
165: (example take-from [one-lot 1 0 9] [one-lot false])
166: ;; taking at :expires is refused
167: (example take-from [one-lot 1 1 10] [one-lot false])
168: ;; a partial take leaves the rest
169: (example take-from [one-lot 1 2 9]
170:          [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 1 :expires 10 :status :active}} :next-id 2} true])
171: 
172: ;; purge takes a lot at its expiry, whatever its status
173: (example purge [one-lot 10] {:lots {} :next-id 2})
174: (example purge [{:lots {1 {:id 1 :sku 4 :qty 3 :expires 10 :status :quarantined}}
175:                  :next-id 2} 10]
176:          {:lots {} :next-id 2})
177: (example purge [one-lot 9] one-lot)

input.content:
# Notes on the stock/picking writ specs

## What was hard to say

**The index base of the report.** TASK says `:filled`, `:short` and `:picks`
hold "the lines' indexes". It never says whether the first line is index 0 or
1. Since an order is a vector and the only index Clojure has is the vector
position, the specs fix **0-based** indexes, and the examples in
`picking.core-spec` (`:filled [0]`, `:picks [[1 2 1]]`) anchor that. If the
intended meaning were 1-based, every `:filled`/`:short`/`:picks` law and
example would move by one; nothing else would change.

**The component's meaning has to be restated, not called.** The picking spec
builds on the stock spec, so `pick` must fill "through `stock.core/take-from`".
But a spec helper may not call the component's fns — a model that did would
judge the workflow by the very code it builds on, and the spec must load and
check before `stock.core` exists. So the component is restated in the picking
spec's own words: `usable?`, `live`, `ordered`, `model-take`, and the models
`model-plan` and `model-pick`. The target's `plan` and `pick` are then pinned by
exact equality with those models. This is a deliberate duplication of the
component's semantics in the spec, and it is the only way to say "what
`take-from` does to a lot" without calling `take-from`.

**"Each through `take-from`" is a call-graph fact, not a value fact.** The
equality to `model-pick` says what `pick` returns, but a semantically equivalent
implementation could inline the lot arithmetic and never call the component. No
law can see the difference, so the structural half is stated separately:
`(calls pick {:through [stock.core/take-from]})`. That is the strongest form
available — it says the target reaches the component, not that every single
pick goes through it. A requirement of "exactly one `take-from` call per pick"
is not expressible in a writ spec.

**"Never partly filled" is expressed by omission.** Nothing in the laws says
"do not partly fill a short line"; the model simply records no pick for a nil
plan, and the exact equality makes any partial fill a mismatch. The intent (a
short line takes *nothing*) only lives in the fact that the model has no branch
that would take part of it.

**`receive` when `:next-id` collides with an existing key.** TASK says a lot is
added "under `:next-id`" and `receive` is then described by `assoc`, so the law
describes the assoc (an overwrite) rather than asserting a fresh key. Generated
stocks do not have to satisfy "every key is below `:next-id`", so the spec does
not smuggle in that invariant.

**The `:lots` type.** `(Index :id Lot)` is used for the lots map, which also
makes the generated stocks well formed (each lot sits under its own `:id`). The
`{:lots {id lot}}` notation suggests exactly this, but it is stronger than the
bare map type; the Index says the key *is* the lot's `:id`, which every law then
relies on.

## What could not be proved (and is only tested)

* `purge-drops-the-expired` — `purge` folds a map of unknown size
  (`reduce-kv`), and the prover does not model that fold (`:require :tested`,
  reason recorded).
* `plan-is-the-greedy-first-expiring` and `pick-fills-every-line-it-can` —
  they order a filtered map of unknown size (`sort-by`) and thread a stock
  through a fold over the order; the prover found no proof (`:require :tested`,
  reasons recorded).

Everything else asks for proof: the stock spec proves 21 of 22 laws (6 for
every input), and the picking spec proves all of its examples. The three tested
laws each ran on 1000+ generated inputs.

## What the reports did not say

Across several runs neither implementation had a test that only ever went one
way: the report's one-sided-branch notes were empty, and the gap check rejected

{"content": "# Notes on the stock/picking writ specs

## What was hard to say

**The index base of the report.** TASK says `:filled`, `:short` and `:picks`
hold "the lines' indexes". It never says whether the first line is index 0 or
1. Since an order is a vector and the only index Clojure has is the vector
position, the specs fix **0-based** indexes, and the examples in
`picking.core-spec` (`:filled [0]`, `:picks [[1 2 1]]`) anchor that. If the
intended meaning were 1-based, every `:filled`/`:short`/`:picks` law and
example would move by one; nothing else would change.

**The component's meaning has to be restated, not called.** The picking spec
builds on the stock spec, so `pick` must fill "through `stock.core/take-from`".
But a spec helper may not call the component's fns — a model that did would
judge the workflow by the very code it builds on, and the spec must load and
check before `stock.core` exists. So the component is restated in the picking
spec's own words: `usable?`, `live`, `ordered`, `model-take`, and the models
`model-plan` and `model-pick`. The target's `plan` and `pick` are then pinned by
exact equality with those models. This is a deliberate duplication of the
component's semantics in the spec, and it is the only way to say "what
`take-from` does to a lot" without calling `take-from`.

**"Each through `take-from`" is a call-graph fact, not a value fact.** The
equality to `model-pick` says what `pick` returns, but a semantically equivalent
implementation could inline the lot arithmetic and never call the component. No
law can see the difference, so the structural half is stated separately:
`(calls pick {:through [stock.core/take-from]})`. That is the strongest form
available — it says the target reaches the component, not that every single
pick goes through it. A requirement of "exactly one `take-from` call per pick"
is not expressible in a writ spec.

**"Never partly filled" is expressed by omission.** Nothing in the laws says
"do not partly fill a short line"; the model simply records no pick for a nil
plan, and the exact equality makes any partial fill a mismatch. The intent (a
short line takes *nothing*) only lives in the fact that the model has no branch
that would take part of it.

**`receive` when `:next-id` collides with an existing key.** TASK says a lot is
added "under `:next-id`" and `receive` is then described by `assoc`, so the law
describes the assoc (an overwrite) rather than asserting a fresh key. Generated
stocks do not have to satisfy "every key is below `:next-id`", so the spec does
not smuggle in that invariant.

**The `:lots` type.** `(Index :id Lot)` is used for the lots map, which also
makes the generated stocks well formed (each lot sits under its own `:id`). The
`{:lots {id lot}}` notation suggests exactly this, but it is stronger than the
bare map type; the Index says the key *is* the lot's `:id`, which every law then
relies on.

## What could not be proved (and is only tested)

* `purge-drops-the-expired` — `purge` folds a map of unknown size
  (`reduce-kv`), and the prover does not model that fold (`:require :tested`,
  reason recorded).
* `plan-is-the-greedy-first-expiring` and `pick-fills-every-line-it-can` —
  they order a filtered map of unknown size (`sort-by`) and thread a stock
  through a fold over the order; the prover found no proof (`:require :tested`,
  reasons recorded).

Everything else asks for proof: the stock spec proves 21 of 22 laws (6 for
every input), and the picking spec proves all of its examples. The three tested
laws each ran on 1000+ generated inputs.

## What the reports did not say

Across several runs neither implementation had a test that only ever went one
way: the report's one-sided-branch notes were empty, and the gap check rejected
impostors (constant, pass-through, off-example and perturbed stand-ins) for
every signed fn. To check the specs are not merely strong on paper, deliberately
broken implementations were tried and each was rejected by the expected law:
`receive` allowing qty 0, `purge` using `<` instead of `<=`, `plan` breaking the
lowest-id tie, `plan` returning what it can instead of nil, and `pick` reporting
1-based indexes.

Done. `bin/check` exits 0. Here's a summary of the work.

## What was delivered

- `test/stock/core_spec.clj` — writ spec for `stock.core`
- `test/picking/core_spec.clj` — writ spec for `picking.core`, built on `stock.core-spec` via `{:uses [stock.core-spec]}`
- `src/stock/core.clj`, `src/picking/core.clj` — plain Clojure implementations
- `NOTES.md` — what was hard to say and what couldn't be expressed
- Commits: `specs` (a70824c, before any code), `implementation` (e85a811), then the proof-strengthening spec change (8287086)

## How the specs capture TASK

- **stock.core**: `usable?` is stated once (`:active`, `qty ≥ 1`, `now < :expires`). Each fn is pinned by an exact model law — `receive` (the assoc under `:next-id`, the increment, qty 0 leaving `[s nil]`), `available` (sum of live lots), `quarantine`/`release`, `take-from` (accept exactly when usable and `1 ≤ n ≤ qty`, removal at 0, otherwise `[s false]`), `purge` (`:expires ≤ now`).
- **picking.core**: `plan` and `pick` are pinned by exact equality to the spec's own `model-plan`/`model-pick` (first-expiring, lowest id on ties, each lot consumed before the next, last pick only what's needed, `[]` for n 0, nil when short, and a nil-plan line taking nothing). `(calls pick {:through [stock.core/take-from]})` enforces the structural requirement that filling goes through the component.
- Boundaries are anchored with examples: `now = :expires` expired, qty 0 unusable, take exactly the whole lot vs. one more, purge at equality, short-line-leaves-the-lot, qty-0 line filled.

## Spec changes made after the initial `specs` commit, and why

1. **Fixed one example before the commit** (`example pick` short-line): its expected stock wrongly omitted the untouched short line's lot. The example was wrong about TASK ("a line whose plan is nil … takes nothing"), so it was corrected — not weakened.
2. **Asked for proof after the code passed**: `(spec stock.core {:require :proved})` and `(spec picking.core {:require :proved …})`. The law statements are unchanged; this only demands proof. Three laws the prover cannot discharge are exempted with recorded reasons (`purge-drops-the-expired`; `plan-is-the-greedy-first-expiring`; `pick-fills-every-line-it-can`) using `{:require :tested :because …}`. This is a strengthening relative to the committed specs, not a weakening.

## Validation

- Three default-seed runs plus `--seed 42` all exit 0; no one-sided-branch notes appeared (every code branch was taken both ways).
- Every signed fn rejects impostors (constant/pass-through/off-example/perturbed).
- Deliberately broken implementations were each rejected by the expected law: `receive` allowing qty 0, `purge` using `<`, `plan` breaking the lowest-id tie, `plan` partially filling instead of nil, and `pick` reporting 1-based indexes.

## Judgment call worth flagging

TASK never states the index base for `:filled`/`:short`/`:picks`. I fixed it to **0-based** (the vector position), anchored by examples, and documented this in `NOTES.md`. If 1-based was intended, only those index values would shift.
